what: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, the US and Israel’s unlikely choice to lead Iran

clean_source_blocks.text: Populist former president’s falling-out with the Tehran regime allegedly drew him into a takeover plot US and Israel hoped to install Ahmadinejad as Iran’s leader For all their outward differences, there always seemed to be things that linked Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Donald Trump. A visit to the then Iranian president’s rather humble Tehran neighbourhood nearly 20 years ago highlighted cost of living problems that prefigured those facing Trump now. Continue reading...

Populist former president’s falling-out with the Tehran regime allegedly drew him into a takeover plot US and Israel hoped to install Ahmadinejad as Iran’s leader For all their outward differences, there always seemed to be things that linked Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Donald Trump. A visit to the then Iranian president’s rather humble Tehran neighbourhood nearly 20 years ago highlighted cost of living problems that prefigured those facing Trump now. Amid soaring prices, the grocer at the end of Ahmadinejad’s street in the Narmak district was no longer stocking tomatoes, saying customers could not afford them and voicing a wish to close down. Shoppers at a nearby fruit and vegetable market complained at the cost of potatoes, onions and fish.

It seemed to represent a failure on the kitchen table issues that the populist leader had pledged to tackle. Trump critics will surely hear an echo. Two decades later, that reporting trip has uncanny resonance amid reports that Israeli strikes on a security post were designed to free Ahmadinejad from house arrest and lead to his installation as Iran’s new leader. The New York Times, citing official sources, reported that the US and Israel had identified the anti-western and anti-Zionist former president as the person they wanted to lead Iran after the regime’s presumed collapse in their face of their military onslaught. The plan went awry almost immediately. The strikes, on the first day of the war on 28 February, killed the guards and injured Ahmadinejad, who was initially reported by Iranian media to have died.

The former president, it is said, went to ground afterwards, having become “disillusioned” with the US-Israeli scheme. His whereabouts is not known. There are multiple other mysteries as to how such a divisive figure became the poster boy for regime change in what has long been the west’s leading adversary in the Middle East. On one level, a mutual attraction between Trump and Ahmadinejad is not so far-fetched. The pair share a populist, headline grabbing communication style; similarities in their autocratic governing style have also been noted. Cynics may add that the two have a common taste for overturning democratic election results. Compare Ahmadinejad’s hugely controversial 2009 election win – widely assumed to have been stolen – with Trump’s efforts to overturn Joe Biden’s victory in 2020.

Populist former president’s falling-out with the Tehran regime allegedly drew him into a takeover plot

US and Israel hoped to install Ahmadinejad as Iran’s leader

For all their outward differences, there always seemed to be things that linked Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Donald Trump.

A visit to the then Iranian president’s rather humble Tehran neighbourhood nearly 20 years ago highlighted cost of living problems that prefigured those facing Trump now.

Amid soaring prices, the grocer at the end of Ahmadinejad’s street in the Narmak district was no longer stocking tomatoes, saying customers could not afford them and voicing a wish to close down. Shoppers at a nearby fruit and vegetable market complained at the cost of potatoes, onions and fish.

It seemed to represent a failure on the kitchen table issues that the populist leader had pledged to tackle. Trump critics will surely hear an echo.

Two decades later, that reporting trip has uncanny resonance amid reports that Israeli strikes on a security post were designed to free Ahmadinejad from house arrest and lead to his installation as Iran’s new leader.

The New York Times, citing official sources, reported that the US and Israel had identified the anti-western and anti-Zionist former president as the person they wanted to lead Iran after the regime’s presumed collapse in their face of their military onslaught.

The plan went awry almost immediately. The strikes, on the first day of the war on 28 February, killed the guards and injured Ahmadinejad, who was initially reported by Iranian media to have died.

The former president, it is said, went to ground afterwards, having become “disillusioned” with the US-Israeli scheme. His whereabouts is not known.

There are multiple other mysteries as to how such a divisive figure became the poster boy for regime change in what has long been the west’s leading adversary in the Middle East.

On one level, a mutual attraction between Trump and Ahmadinejad is not so far-fetched. The pair share a populist, headline grabbing communication style; similarities in their autocratic governing style have also been noted.

Cynics may add that the two have a common taste for overturning democratic election results. Compare Ahmadinejad’s hugely controversial 2009 election win – widely assumed to have been stolen – with Trump’s efforts to overturn Joe Biden’s victory in 2020.

payload.title: Väitteet nostavat Ahmadinejadin yllättävään rooliin Iran-suunnitelmissa
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin kerrotaan pitäneen Iranin entistä presidenttiä Mahmoud Ahmadinejadia mahdollisena johtajana tilanteessa, jossa Teheranin hallinto olisi horjunut sotilaallisen paineen alla.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin kerrotaan tunnistaneen Iranin entisen presidentin Mahmoud Ahmadinejadin henkilöksi, jonka ne olisivat halunneet johtavan Irania Teheranin hallinnon mahdollisen romahduksen jälkeen. Väitteiden mukaan suunnitelma liittyi iskuun turvallisuuskohteeseen, jonka tarkoituksena oli vapauttaa Ahmadinejad kotiarestista. Hanke näyttää kuitenkin kariutuneen heti alkuvaiheessa, sillä iskuissa kuoli vartijoita ja Ahmadinejad haavoittui.

## Entinen presidentti yllättävässä asetelmassa

Ahmadinejad johti Irania vuosina, jolloin hän tuli tunnetuksi populistisesta tyylistään, länsivastaisuudestaan ja Israelia jyrkästi vastustaneesta retoriikastaan. Siksi väite siitä, että Yhdysvallat ja Israel olisivat nähneet hänet mahdollisena hallinnonvaihdon johtohahmona, on poliittisesti poikkeuksellinen.

Taustalla kerrotaan olleen Ahmadinejadin välirikko Teheranin nykyisen valtakoneiston kanssa. Entinen presidentti oli ajautunut sivuun vallasta, ja hänen asemansa oli heikentynyt niin paljon, että häntä kuvataan olleen kotiarestissa. Raportoidun suunnitelman mukaan Israelin iskut turvallisuusasemaan olisivat avanneet tien hänen vapauttamiselleen ja nostamiselleen näkyvään rooliin.

Suunnitelma epäonnistui väitteiden mukaan nopeasti. Iskujen kerrotaan tapahtuneen sodan ensimmäisenä päivänä 28. helmikuuta. Vartijoita kuoli, Ahmadinejad loukkaantui, ja iranilaismediassa hänen kerrottiin aluksi jopa kuolleen. Myöhemmin hänen sanotaan kadonneen julkisuudesta, eikä hänen olinpaikkaansa tiedetä.

## Populismi yhdisti, politiikka erotti

Ahmadinejadin mahdollinen valinta on herättänyt kysymyksiä myös siksi, että hän on pitkään ollut lännen näkökulmasta hyvin kiistanalainen hahmo. Hänen poliittinen tyylinsä rakentui voimakkaiden puheiden, vastakkainasettelun ja kansaan vetoavan esiintymisen varaan.

Vertailuja on tehty myös Donald Trumpiin. Molempien on katsottu hyödyntäneen populistista viestintää ja suoraa, otsikoihin sopivaa poliittista tyyliä. Samalla molempien poliittiseen historiaan liittyy kiistoja vaalituloksista: Ahmadinejadin vuoden 2009 vaalivoittoa pidettiin laajasti epäselvänä, kun taas Trump pyrki kumoamaan Joe Bidenin voiton vuoden 2020 presidentinvaaleissa.

Iranin sisäpolitiikan kannalta väitteet korostavat sitä, miten vaikeasti ennakoitavia hallinnonvaihtoon liittyvät ulkopuoliset suunnitelmat voivat olla. Ahmadinejad oli entinen vallankäyttäjä, mutta myös jakava ja nykyjohdon kanssa riitautunut poliitikko. Juuri tämä yhdistelmä näyttää tehneen hänestä sekä mahdollisen työkalun että epävarman valinnan.
